name: hydra
plain: `hydra` tries many usernames and passwords against a live service (SSH, FTP, HTTP forms, RDP, SMB, databases...) until one works. This is online guessing, so it is slow compared with cracking a hash, and it can lock accounts or trigger alarms.
Use it only in labs and tests where you have written permission. It is a classic CTF tool when a service has a weak password and you have a username or a wordlist.
when: Guess an SSH or FTP login in a lab.
Test a web login form in a challenge.
Check whether a service accepts weak or default passwords.

examples.title: One user, wordlist of passwords (SSH)
examples.explain: -l is a single login name, -P a password list. The service and target form the last argument.

examples.title: Many users, many passwords
examples.explain: -L is a user list. Hydra tries combinations; keep lists short because online guessing is slow.

examples.title: Limit threads (be gentle)
examples.explain: -t sets parallel tasks. SSH servers drop many connections, so 4 is wise.

examples.title: A web login form
examples.explain: Three parts separated by colons: the path, the body with ^USER^ and ^PASS^ as placeholders, and the failure text (F=). Hydra treats a reply without the failure text as a success.

examples.title: Stop at the first success
examples.explain: -f stops after the first working login.

examples.title: Try a blank, same-as-login and reversed password
examples.explain: -e n tries empty passwords, s tries the login as password, r tries it reversed. Cheap and often works on weak accounts.

examples.title: Colon-separated list
examples.explain: -C reads user:password pairs, good for default credential lists.

options.plain: A single login name / a file of login names.
A single password / a file of passwords.
Try n (null), s (same as login), r (reversed login).
Wait time for replies / between connections per task.
Stop at the first found login (per host / overall).
Loop over users first, not passwords.
Write found logins to a file.
Show details about a service module.

mistakes: Locking real accounts: online guessing triggers lockout policies.
Too many tasks: SSH refuses and hydra reports false failures.
A wrong failure string in http-post-form: hydra then reports every password as valid.
Not capturing the real request first: check the form with the browser or curl.
Using it where you have no permission.
try: Set up a lab SSH user with a weak password and find it with a short list.
Read the module help with hydra -U http-post-form.
Compare -t 4 and -t 16 on a lab SSH server.
see_also: john(8), hashcat(1), medusa(1), ncrack(1), nmap(1), curl(1), and the wordlists in /usr/share/wordlists.
captured_with: Examples are written to explain a technique; they are not captured output.
